Subject: Colo pod segmentation & HA handoff

Hi all,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our current reference for the colo pod segmentation we plan to hand to EdgeColo next week. High level goals: reduce blast radius between tenant slices, enable per-pod canary traffic policies, and provide an N+1 HA pattern for control-plane proxies.

What I need from the group this week:
- EdgeColo: confirm whether the per-pod /28 allocation works for your on-rack CPEs and whether BGP sessions are preferred or static routes.
- ACME (Sara): confirm rack power constraints and suggested maintenance windows for the cutover.
- Infra (Jonas/Kim): review segmentation diagram and call out any firewall/service ACL gaps.

Attached: colo-segmentation-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram), pod-ha-handbook-v0.9.md (checklist).

Proposed short call: Wed 05/05 14:00 PT (30m) to walk diagram and actions. Let me know conflicts.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
[lukas_meyer@redwood.ai]

Hi Lukas / team,

Thanks for the doc. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- /28 per pod is fine, but we prefer eBGP peering where we control the next-hop (operationally simpler for our fabric).
- Can you confirm which ASN you'll present and whether you'll do unique ASNs per customer slice or use a shared ASN with community tagging?
- For HA: are you expecting us to perform any active health-checking of your control-plane proxies, or will failover be entirely internal to your pod (we need to know for automations on our side).

We can join Wed 05/05 14:00 PT.

--
EdgeColo Ops
ops@edgecolo.com
[Attachment: none]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeColo Ops <ops@edgecolo.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Colo pod segmentation & HA handoff

Thanks, good questions. Short answers up-front:
- We'll present ASN 64512 (shared across pods) and use BGP community tags to isolate tenant routes.
- Failover: primary plan is internal N+1 for control-plane proxies; EdgeColo can query our /health endpoints for additional automation if you want to trigger re-routing on your fabric.

I attached an updated diagram (v2) with explicit BGP session points and a small table showing expected prefixes and community ranges. Also called out the control-plane probe endpoints (port 8443) and suggested probe timings.

Open items I flagged in the diagram:
1) Firewall ACLs between management VLAN and tenant slice (need ops confirmation on allowed source ranges).
2) Cert rotation flow for proxies when pods are pre-provisioned vs hot-provisioned.
3) Expected maintenance window (ACME to confirm).

On the Wed call let's lock down items 1 and 2 so EdgeColo can prepare their playbook.

Jonas
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Copying the operational checklist from pod-ha-handbook-v0.9 and calling out what we need to validate before handoff: 

- IP plan validation: confirm /28 allocations mapped to rack ports (EdgeColo).
- ACL review: EdgeColo to provide explicit allowed source ranges for management VLAN.
- BGP params: Jonas to confirm TTL and AS-path prepend guidance (we prefer a TTL of 2 for the eBGP sessions).
- Health checks: provide /health endpoints and expected behaviour during rolling upgrades.
- Cert rotation: Irene to detail rotation steps and intended KMS integration points.
- Cutover runbook: include a rollback path and traffic smoke tests (Tessa to author smoke test checklist).

Irene — can you draft the certificate rotation sequence (short bullets) and drop it in the Drive link? We'll add it to the playbook before the Wed call.

Kimberly Park
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
